Assertions.Description: The actual Settings launch control opens a titled editor; record new process/window identity.
The resulting editor is not elevated.
System-variable editing controls are disabled.
System Add is disabled.
User Add is available.
Administrator launch on opens the editor through Settings.
The actual editor token is elevated.
System-variable editing is enabled.
System Add is enabled; no arbitrary machine writes are needed.
Both disabled and enabled choices persist in the stored module flag and match the Settings toggle after save; no Settings close/reopen is required.
Unrelated module flags remain unchanged at both transitions.
Reopened OOBE Launch is disabled when this module is disabled.
Reopened OOBE Launch is enabled when this module is enabled.
Invoking the OOBE control actually opens the editor.
Enabled Environment Variables tile opens the editor; signaling the module directly is not entry evidence.
Native Environment Variables dialog contains the exact added name/value.
Applied variables contains the exact added name/value.
HKCU contains the expected value; record its raw kind.
Native dialog shows `two` in exactly one matching row.
Applied variables shows `two` without a duplicate.
HKCU contains `two` under the same name.
Native dialog no longer contains the owned variable.
Applied variables no longer contains the owned variable.
The owned HKCU value is absent, not an empty string.
Native System scope shows the added exact name/value.
Applied variables shows the added System variable.
HKLM holds the expected added value/kind; no User-scope value was created.
Native System scope shows the edited value without duplicates.
Applied variables shows the edited System value.
HKLM holds `two`; no User-scope write occurred.
Native System scope no longer contains the owned name.
Applied variables no longer contains the owned name.
Owned HKLM value absent and User scope unchanged; restore original raw kinds.
P1 appears disabled, has zero variables, and persists in profiles.json.
P1 contains exactly V1=`one` in its row and persisted data after outer Save.
Both P2 variables appear with exact values in the native User dialog.
Both P2 variables appear in Applied variables.
P2 is stored enabled with both variables and their expected HKCU values.
P1 becomes enabled and P2 becomes disabled.
Native dialog removes V2/V3 and shows V1=`one`.
Applied variables removes V2/V3 and shows V1=`one`.
HKCU and saved enablement match the switch.
Native dialog removes the originally absent P1 variables on unapply.
Applied variables removes those P1 variables.
HKCU has no residual P1 variable and saved P1 is disabled.
Existing-variable selection and outer Save store the changed profile value without changing live User state.
Native dialog shows the override and exact named backup containing `original`.
Applied list shows the profile override and User backup.
HKCU override/backup values match; private HKLM comparison remains unchanged.
Native dialog restores `original` and removes the generated backup on unapply.
Applied list restores the original User row and removes the backup.
Original raw text returns, backup absent, HKLM unchanged; exact-kind cleanup remains separate.
Originally absent source becomes `one`; no backup is created for a nonexistent original.
Active edit yields `two` and does not create a spurious backup of the profile's own old value.
Destination is `two`; old source and its backup are absent, not resurrected as `one`.
Source, renamed destination and both backup names are absent after product unapply.
Source becomes `one` and its backup contains the pre-profile `original`.
Source becomes `two`; backup still contains `original`, not `one`.
Old source returns to `original`, destination is `two`, old backup disappears.
Old source remains `original`; absent-baseline destination and generated backups disappear.
At every stage in both variants, the full private HKLM and untracked HKCU maps remain unchanged.
Record selection and Add availability, Save/reopen, and prove unchanged membership/count with no duplicate.
Expanded SYSTEM Path precedes expanded USER Path, separated by semicolon; compare privately.
Outer Save renders and stores three separate PATH entries, not one semicolon string row.
Delete removes only the selected PATH entry.
Move up produces the independently expected order.
Move down produces the independently expected order.
Insert before places the new entry before the selected entry.
Insert after places the new entry after the selected entry.
Save/reopen preserves the final exact order in UI and profile data.
Native dialog shows exact profile User Path and complete original backup value.
Applied PATH is expanded SYSTEM Path plus profile PATH; backup User row is correct.
Raw HKCU Path/backup values match the planned transition; HKLM unchanged.
Normal close/relaunch yields an actual new titled editor process without diagnostic recovery.
Profile IDs/names/variables/enabled state persist in the new UI and file.
Native and Applied observations still match the active profile and backup.
Cancel and dismiss leave the active profile and its environment unchanged.
Confirmed deletion removes P1-owned values, restores originals and removes backups in the native dialog.
Applied list reflects the same deletion/unapply/restoration.
P1 is gone from saved profiles; its variables/backups have the expected baseline-relative state.
Delete P2 through UI; neither owned profile remains in UI/profiles.json, and unrelated profiles are unchanged.
Case, slash direction, trailing separator and expanded-reference input rows collapse equivalents while preserving first spelling/order.
Save/reopen preserves the independently expected deduplicated sequence.
Cancel leaves previous data unchanged.
Non-PATH variable editing exposes no Remove duplicates action.
All P01 rows behave correctly in Add User variable.
All P01 rows behave correctly in Edit User variable.
All P01 rows behave correctly in profile New variable.
All P01 rows behave correctly in profile Edit variable.
All P01 name rows behave correctly in profile Add/Edit name fields; reopening Add starts disabled.
Add User enforces both name and total-entry boundary pairs.
Edit User enforces both boundary pairs.
Profile New variable enforces both boundary pairs.
Profile Edit variable enforces both boundary pairs.
Profile Add/Edit names enforce the 259/260 boundary without a variable-value constraint.
Add User rejects a case-insensitive duplicate.
Edit User rejects another row's name but permits its unchanged self-name.
Profile New variable rejects a case-insensitive duplicate.
Profile Edit variable rejects another member's name but permits its unchanged self-name.
System Add enforces all P01 name/commit-state rows.
System Edit enforces all P01 name/commit-state rows.
System Add enforces both name and total-entry boundary pairs.
System Edit enforces both boundary pairs.
System Add rejects a case-insensitive duplicate.
System Edit rejects another row's name but permits its unchanged self-name.
On every non-admin name surface, control-character names cannot be committed as invalid saved names; distinguish rejection/truncation from model validation.
On User Add/Edit and profile New/Edit variable surfaces, embedded NUL cannot produce an invalid saved value; a truncated valid value does not prove backend NUL rejection.
System Add/Edit cannot commit control-character names as invalid saved names; distinguish provider rejection/truncation from model validation.
System Add/Edit cannot save embedded NUL in a variable value; truncated input is not evidence of backend rejection.
Valid long backup is created with the exact original value and observed in native/Applied UI and HKCU.
Unapply restores the original and removes the long backup across both UI surfaces and storage.
A generated backup exceeding total-entry length 32766 is rejected without partial application or forced invalid registry writes.
Loading the stored active profile with an invalid name disables it.
UI shows the specific invalid-name warning, not a generic applicability message.
Normal launch in the affected language reaches a titled editor without the startup fault.
Authorized elevated launch in that language reaches a titled editor without the startup fault.
Normal launch preserves the Unicode title and opens successfully.
Authorized elevated launch preserves the Unicode title and opens successfully.
An actual external environment-change notification produces the reload notice.
Product self-originated notification does not produce that notice.
An unrelated settings notification does not produce that notice.
Module is initially disabled in Runner.
Module is initially disabled in Settings.
First Save does not unexpectedly flip the initial disabled state.
Invoke the actual Environment Variables command and observe editor arrival.
Invoke its Settings command and observe navigation to this module.
Pin the module command through UI and observe its pinned identity.
Invoking that pinned command opens the editor.
Changing this command's fallback setting leaves another command's setting unchanged; restore both and original pins/order.
Environment Variables commands in the PowerToys extension use the selected localized labels.
Caption-button glyphs remain visible with correct foreground in light theme.
Caption-button glyphs remain visible with correct foreground in dark theme.
Module labels match the selected translations.
Dialog actions match the selected translations; restore original locale.
Owned module actions produce corresponding utility events visible in the viewer; restore prior collection settings without disclosing unrelated event content.
